category_title: High-intelligence elementary student with inattentive ADHD and executive functioning deficits
minimal_context: Gail is transitioning from putting away a poster board project to starting a science experiment.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Please put your poster board away with the other projects, and then we will begin today's science experiment. I've also explained when the extra credit is due.

STUDENT: (Takes an inordinate amount of time to put her poster board with the other projects along the wall closest to her desk)

TUTOR: Gail, please finish putting that away and start working on the assignment.

STUDENT: (Takes quite a long time to hand it in and misses part of the instructions regarding the test)

TUTOR: You need to start the experiment now. Do you know what to do?

STUDENT: The hardest thing in school today was science. I wasn’t sure what steps to do in our experiment and I’m not sure when the extra credit is due, either.

options.A: Provide verbal warnings of the upcoming transition from the poster board to the science experiment.
options.B: Put off the planned science experiment and wait until the student finishes putting away the poster board.
options.C: Terminate the academic demands and remove the science experiment materials from the desk for 10 seconds.
options.D: Work with the student one-on-one, assisting her to get organized and focused on the science experiment.
